confidence_notes: Page 1 = title page (Three Tone-Pictures cover + contents list), page 2 = Yeats epigraph page for No.1 (front matter). Music for 'The Lake at Evening' occupies PDF pages 3-5 only (17 total systems... actually 12 systems: 4+4+4). Page 6 is a Schirmer house ad ('Four Interesting Piano Pieces'), page 7 is blank, page 8 is another house ad ('Four Piano Pieces by Paolo Conte') - Nos. 2 'The Vale of Dreams' and 3 'The Night Winds' are NOT present anywhere in this scan (the IMSLP file only reproduces No.1 despite the title page listing all three); all of pages 1,2,6,7,8 = zero anchors. No printed measure numbers anywhere on pages 3-5, so every anchor's measure number was obtained by chaining bar-by-bar from m1 (confirmed full 3/4 bar via XML duration sums), using MusicXML clef-change/dynamic/rhythm landmarks to pin system-start measures rather than relying on raw barline pixel-counts alone (dense chordal texture made pure visual barline counting unreliable in isolation; cross-checked with a python column-darkness barline detector on pages 4-5 which corroborated measure counts for systems with unambiguous landmarks on both ends - page4 system3 (m36-39, bounded by 'poco agitato' text landmark and m40's 'f + rests' landmark) and system4 (m40-47, bounded by m40 landmark and page5's 'Tempo I' m48 landmark) - both counts are solidly landmark-bounded on both sides). Page3's yTopPct/yCenterPct are visual crop-based estimates (±0.02-0.03) rather than clean programmatic staff-line detection: automated row-darkness clustering, which worked cleanly on pages 4-5 (full 5-line-staff clusters found at consistent thresholds), returned only partial/noisy clusters on page 3 - likely due to lighter print density in that scan region (system 1 has two RH whole-bar rests with sparse ink) or slight scan skew; page3's measure-number assignments themselves are high-confidence (each boundary confirmed via a clef-change, rest, or rhythmic-signature landmark against the MusicXML), only the pixel y-position is the lower-confidence part there, hence low_confidence:true on all 4 page-3 anchors. Page4 and page5 yTopPct/yCenterPct come from clean programmatic staff-line row-detection (150dpi row-darkness clustering, full 5-line staff clusters found for every system) and are high confidence. Page5 systems 2-4 (measures 54, 59, 63) are marked low_confidence on the MEASURE field: the coda (m54-67) is a long repeated ostinato/pedal-tone passage where RH and LH alternate an near-identical 'E E Q E E' / 'Q E E Q' figure for 14 measures, making sub-measure identity hard to pin from shape alone; these three boundaries rely on: m58's LH clef-change-to-treble coinciding with an '8...pp' ottava restart (used to place the system2/3 seam at m58/59), and m64's ppp dynamic (used to place the system3/4 seam at m62/63, assuming ppp falls on the 2nd measure of system4). Both are plausible and self-consistent with the closed total (6+5+4+5=20 measures on page5, matching 67-47=20), but could plausibly be off by one measure at either seam if the ppp/ottava placement assumption is wrong. Continuity chain: 1,6,12,18,24,30,36,40,48,54,59,63 with implied per-system bar counts 5,6,6,6,6,6,4,8,6,5,4,5 - sums to exactly 67 and PASSES the closure check (63+5-1=67).
